subject: general
question: By how many places has India improved its ranking in the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in the 2025 edition of the Sustainable Development Report compared to 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**10**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Report (SDR)** is an annual assessment that tracks the progress of all **193 UN Member States** toward achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• In the **2025 edition** of the report, **India** demonstrated a significant advancement by improving its global ranking by **10 positions** compared to the **2024** data.
 
• This improvement reflects **India’s** concerted efforts in areas such as **climate action (Goal 13)**, **clean energy (Goal 7)**, and **sustainable cities (Goal 11)**, which have seen measurable positive shifts in the latest reporting cycle.
 
• The report is published by the **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**, which has been operating under the auspices of the **UN Secretary-General** since **2012**.
 
• The **2025 ranking** highlights that while **India** still faces challenges in **gender equality (Goal 5)** and **hunger (Goal 2)**, the overall trajectory has moved upward, moving the nation closer to the median ranking of **developing economies**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 10.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**

 
 
• The **SDGs**, also known as the **Global Goals**, were adopted by the **United Nations** in **September 2015** as a universal call to action to end poverty and protect the planet.
 
• There are **17 Goals** and **169 targets** intended to be reached by the year **2030**.
 
• These goals replaced the **Millennium Development Goals (MDGs)** which ended in **2015**.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog’s SDG India Index:**
 
 
• At the national level, **NITI Aayog** is the nodal agency responsible for monitoring **SDG** implementation through the **SDG India Index**.
 
• The index ranks **States** and **Union Territories** based on their performance, categorizing them as **Aspirants**, **Performers**, **Front-Runners**, or **Achievers**.
 
• The latest **SDG India Index 2023-24** showed that **Kerala** and **Uttarakhand** emerged as top-performing states.
 
 
 
• **SDSN and Global Monitoring:**
 
 
• The **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)** is led by world-renowned economist **Professor Jeffrey Sachs**.
 
• The **Sustainable Development Report** includes the **SDG Index** and **Dashboards**, which provide a visual representation of a country's progress (green, yellow, orange, or red) for each goal.
 
• The report emphasizes the **SDG Stimulus**, a plan to scale up affordable long-term financing for **sustainable development** in **developing nations**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Ranking Context:**

 
 
• In the **Sustainable Development Report 2024**, **India** was ranked **109th** out of **167 countries**.
 
• The jump of **10 places** in the **2025 edition** signifies one of the largest single-year improvements for the country since the **2030 Agenda** began.
 
 
 
• **Key Pillars of Improvement:**
 
 
• The improvement in **India’s** score is largely driven by **Goal 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production)** and **Goal 13 (Climate Action)**, where **India** is on track to meet several national targets ahead of the **2030** deadline.
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana** and **Jal Jeevan Mission** are cited as critical governmental interventions that have bolstered **India’s** performance in **health** and **sanitation** goals.
